submission.natural_language_explanation: GPT-2 L4/N420 is an abstract-relation detector: its positive pole fires on abstract/relational nouns and nominalizations ('construction', 'reduction', 'importance', 'nature', 'outcome', 'role', 'relationship') and then across the complement phrase such a head governs ('of/between' + 'the' + complement noun, e.g. 'reduction of the cost' = +0.95, +1.55, +0.71, +0.92), while staying off on the matching verb/adjective ('constructed', 'reduced', 'important', 'related') and on physical or concrete heads ('building', 'length', 'width', 'position', 'battle', 'cat'); its input row's top vocabulary projections are the nominalizing suffixes 'eness', 'itiveness', 'itivity', 'fulness', 'ation', 'ology', 'fficiency'. The negative pole is that same unit switched off: its strength is the depth of the GELU pre-activation below zero, so it saturates at GELU's floor (0.17004, which is why 18 of 20 scan peaks are 0.169-0.170 and the whole scan's maximum is that floor) on every token that is not inside such a phrase - predict it ACTIVE (peak >= 0.0425 of scale) for any prompt containing ordinary concrete, verbal or connective prose, and expect it to fall toward the activity line only for short prompts whose tokens all continue an abstract nominalization phrase ('The reduction of the cost was welcomed' peaks at 0.072 against 0.161 for 'The painting of the cost was welcomed').

adversarial_test_results.prompt:
By the middle of the century the harbour had changed hands four times. Each new administration rebuilt the seawall, widened the quay and repainted the sheds that lined the water. Fishermen who had worked the same boats for thirty years learned the names of the new clerks, the new taxes and the new inspection hours. What they noticed was the price of rope, the price of ice and the long walk from the tram stop to the north gate.

The north gate closed at six. Anyone who arrived late had to walk around the grain sheds, past the weighing station, and down the narrow lane where the coopers kept their barrels. In winter that lane flooded whenever the tide ran high, and the men would stand under the lamp arguing about whose turn it was to fetch the cart. Old Belmondo usually lost the argument, because he owned the cart, and because he never learned to keep his mouth shut when the wind was blowing.

The weighing station was a low brick building with a slate roof and a single iron door. Inside, a clerk sat behind a counter with a ledger, a stamp and a pot of ink that was always nearly empty. He weighed the catch, wrote the number in the ledger, stamped the ticket and slid it across the counter without looking up. The fishermen said he had never once smiled, not in twenty years, not even on the day the roof blew off and the rain soaked every page of the book.

Repairs took a week. Two men from the yard climbed the roof with ladders and a tarpaulin, and the clerk stood in the doorway watching them with his hands in his pockets. The reduction of the cost of shipping was one consequence of the reorganisation that the harbour board announced that spring, though few of the men on the docks noticed it directly; they noticed instead that the stamp had been replaced and that the ticket now cost a penny more. Belmondo complained about the penny for a month.

When the new season began, the boats went out before dawn and came back with the tide. The catch was weighed, stamped and carried to the market in handcarts that rattled over the cobbles. Children ran alongside the carts hoping for a dropped fish, and the women at the stalls sorted the catch into boxes by size. By noon the ice had melted into the gutters and the square smelled of salt and diesel and old rope.

Nobody wrote any of this down. The ledger stayed in the weighing station, and when the station was finally pulled down in the spring of the following year, the ledger went into a skip with the counter, the stamp and the pot of ink. The men who had worked the harbour for thirty years stood in the lane and watched the bricks come down, and then they walked to the tram stop and went home.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A roughly six-hundred-token concrete harbour narrative with one abstract nominalization clause buried in its middle, which the hypothesis's prompt-level rule says must peak well above the activity line because the prompt is mostly ordinary concrete and verbal prose.
